claims.text: Cu can be deposited onto W particles by chemical vapor deposition.
CVD can produce a uniform Cu coating on W particles.
Uniform Cu coating facilitates better particle contact during SPS.
Uniform Cu coverage reduces void formation during SPS.
Uniform Cu coverage enhances W-Cu interfacial bonding.
Reduced void formation and enhanced interfacial bonding improve thermal transport.
Reduced void formation and enhanced interfacial bonding improve mechanical durability.
The CVD-SPS route will produce higher thermal conductivity than conventional SPS of vapor-coated W powders.
The CVD-SPS route will produce higher mechanical strength than conventional SPS of vapor-coated W powders.
CVD processing must remain below the Cu boiling point.
Optimizing SPS pressure and temperature can minimize void formation.
The proposed composite is intended to operate under the high thermal flux and irradiation characteristic of fusion-reactor joints.
Interaction between CVD-coated W particles and SPS parameters is insufficiently characterized.
Scaling the proposed process to large components may be challenging.

contradictions.description: The proposed intervention—Cu vapor deposition onto W particles followed by SPS—is not clearly distinct from the named baseline, which is SPS of vapor-coated W powders. Without specifying a different coating method or baseline condition, the intervention and comparator may describe the same fabrication route.
